eyebrow: Every RUN, COPY, and ADD is a layer
code:
FROM node:20-slim      # layer 1
WORKDIR /app             # layer 2
COPY package.json ./     # layer 3
RUN npm install           # layer 4
COPY . .                  # layer 5
caption: Each layer is cached by its instruction plus its inputs -- nothing changed, nothing rebuilds.

eyebrow: A cache hit -- only the code changed
code:
$ docker build -t northbridge/catalog:1.4 .
 => CACHED [3/5] COPY package.json package-lock.json ./
 => CACHED [4/5] RUN npm install --production
 => [5/5] COPY . .
caption: package.json didn't change, so Docker reuses the cached install step -- a 2-second build instead of 18.

eyebrow: A cache miss -- one change invalidates everything after
code:
$ docker build -t northbridge/catalog:1.4 .
 => [3/5] COPY package.json package-lock.json ./
 => [4/5] RUN npm install --production
 => [5/5] COPY . .
caption: package.json changed this time -- every layer stacked after it reruns too, even the unchanged COPY . ..

steps.label: package.json first
steps.sub: changes rarely -- keeps the expensive install step cached

steps.label: npm install
steps.sub: the slow step, protected as long as dependencies are unchanged

steps.label: COPY . . last
steps.sub: application code changes constantly -- isolate that churn to the final layer

subtitle: Two ways to set what a container runs -- and why Northbridge sometimes combines them.
